title: Herman Gunter III, et al. v. Central Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The full SJC denied the complaint, holding that the Session could disapprove the complainants for ruling elder based on theological views it judged unacceptable or harmful to the church and could consider divisiveness. The Presbytery’s annulment of the Session’s categorical statement that theonomy violated WCF 19.4 was not disturbed.
first_summary: Two ruling-elder nominees challenged the Session’s refusal to approve them because of their theonomic views and perceived divisiveness. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that a church court may assess disputed theological views and their effect on the church’s peace, purity, and progress. It deferred to the court of original jurisdiction because the broader church had not clearly defined theonomy, while expressly declining to decide whether theonomy itself was acceptable.
summary: Two ruling-elder nominees challenged the Session’s refusal to approve them based on their theonomic views and perceived divisiveness. The full SJC denied the complaint, holding that the court of original jurisdiction may assess an unsettled theological position and whether it threatens the church’s peace, purity, or progress; divisiveness was therefore properly considered. The ruling did not decide the merits of theonomy itself, and it left undisturbed Presbytery’s annulment of the Session’s categorical statement that theonomy violated WCF 19.4.

sources.supports: Assembly adoption, challenged actions, full SJC judgment, reasoning, and express limitation.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Canonical caption and docket appear at lines 1 and 13-15; the Assembly approved the judgment at lines 9-11.
evidence_notes.dispute: The Session disapproved the nominees because of theonomy and barred theonomic teaching; Presbytery denied their complaint but annulled the categorical WCF 19.4 statement (lines 19-43; printed pp. 198-199).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The full SJC answered both issues yes and denied the complaint (lines 45-55), reasoning that original-jurisdiction courts may assess unsettled theology and its effect on peace, purity, or progress (lines 59-102, 124-145; printed pp. 199-201).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The SJC expressly declined to decide theonomy itself (lines 149-151). The concurrence’s procedural concerns were separate (lines 157-241), and the panel’s contrary answer on divisiveness was not affirmed (lines 243-257).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No judgment was incorporated by reference. Prior General Assembly actions and Case 90-8 were cited as guidance concerning theological examinations (lines 102-145).

source_limits: The source includes the adopted judgment, concurrence, unaffirmed panel judgment, and party briefs, but not the complete underlying record. Allegations in the briefs are not treated as findings.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the refusal to approve ruling-elder nominees and the grounds of theology and divisiveness.
score_reasons.decision: States denial, acceptance of both grounds, and the undisturbed Presbytery annulment.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains deference to the original court on an unsettled theological issue affecting church peace, purity, or progress.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between deciding a local court’s authority and deciding the merits of theonomy.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the full SJC judgment from the concurrence, unaffirmed panel ruling, and party arguments.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts necessary to explain the dispute, result, and limitation.

verification_notes: Rechecked the operative full-SJC judgment at lines 43-55 against the attached panel judgment at lines 243-257. The final summary clarifies that the panel’s negative answer on divisiveness was not affirmed, adds the express refusal to decide theonomy, and notes that Presbytery’s annulment was left undisturbed.
